q: In the three-layer architecture of the Internet of Things, which layer is responsible for sensing physical quantities and identifying objects?
exp: The perception (sensing) layer contains sensors, actuators and tags that collect data from the physical world.

q: Google App Engine, which lets developers deploy their code without managing servers or operating systems, is best classified as:
exp: It provides a platform (runtime and tools) for building applications, which is Platform as a Service.

q: In an IoT system, the middleware layer is mainly responsible for:
options: Generating the radio signal used by sensors
Hiding the heterogeneity of devices and protocols and giving applications a uniform interface
Printing the final reports for end users
Supplying power to the sensor nodes
exp: Middleware sits between devices/network and applications, handling device management, protocol translation, data aggregation and APIs.

q: In the Modbus protocol, which statement is correct?
options: Communication follows a master-slave (client-server) request/response model
Every node publishes messages to a central broker
All nodes can transmit at the same time without any addressing
It was designed mainly for sending e-mail between servers
exp: Modbus is a master-slave request/response protocol: the master starts every transaction and slaves reply.

q: Modbus TCP/IP uses which well-known TCP port?
exp: Modbus TCP uses port 502 (1883 is MQTT, 5683 is CoAP, 80 is HTTP).

q: What is the default TCP port used by an MQTT broker for unencrypted connections?
exp: MQTT uses port 1883 for plain connections; 8883 is used for MQTT over TLS, and 5683 is the CoAP UDP port.

q: What makes the blocks in a blockchain linked together and the chain tamper-evident?
options: Each block stores the IP address of its miner
Each block stores the private key of the sender
Each block stores the hash of the previous block
Each block stores a timestamp of the next block
exp: Changing any block alters its hash and breaks the previous-hash link stored in the next block.

q: A tyre manufacturer sells directly through its web portal to car-making companies. Which e-commerce model does this represent?
exp: Business selling to another business is B2B.

q: Which generation of mobile networks first introduced digital voice transmission (GSM) and SMS text messaging?
exp: 1G was analog; 2G made voice digital and introduced SMS.

q: Using vibration and temperature sensors on factory machines to forecast a failure before it occurs is called:
exp: Predictive maintenance is a flagship IIoT application: sensor data is analysed to predict faults and schedule repair.

q: ZigBee is based on which IEEE standard for low-rate wireless personal area networks?
exp: ZigBee builds its network and application layers on the IEEE 802.15.4 PHY and MAC.

q: A Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor is one that:
options: Runs as an ordinary application on top of a host operating system
Runs directly on the host hardware without a host operating system
Is a physical network switch connecting virtual machines
Is available only as a SaaS product
exp: Type 1 hypervisors such as VMware ESXi and Xen run directly on hardware.

q: The Digital India programme was launched by the Government of India in the year:
exp: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015.

q: Which of the following is a recommended green computing practice?
options: Enabling sleep or power-saving mode on idle computers
Keeping all desktops switched on overnight for updates
Using animated screen savers instead of sleep mode
Throwing old monitors into ordinary household waste
exp: Power management reduces energy consumption of idle systems.

q: Which type of firewall inspects the actual content of application-layer traffic such as HTTP or FTP and is generally the most secure but slowest?
exp: Proxy/application gateways examine application data; packet filters only look at headers (IP, port, protocol).

q: Which statement about passive RFID tags is correct?
options: They carry an internal battery that lets them transmit for kilometres
They work only when connected to a Wi-Fi router
They have no battery and are powered by the reader's radio-frequency field
They require a SIM card to transmit
exp: Passive tags harvest energy from the reader's RF signal to respond.

q: A cloud infrastructure shared by several organizations that have common concerns such as security requirements and compliance policies is called a:
exp: Community cloud serves a specific community of organizations with shared concerns.

q: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) in India was developed by:
exp: UPI was developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).

q: What distinguishes a smart card from a magnetic-stripe card?
options: It contains an embedded microprocessor chip that can store data and perform computations
It can only store a fixed account number
It works only with ATMs of the same bank
exp: A smart card (EMV chip card) carries a microprocessor/memory chip; a magnetic stripe is passive storage and easier to clone.

q: Which pair of components is typical of an industrial control (IIoT/SCADA) environment?
exp: PLCs (programmable logic controllers) control machines and SCADA supervises and acquires data from them.

q: By default, CoAP (Constrained Application Protocol) runs over which transport protocol?
exp: CoAP is a lightweight REST-like protocol designed for constrained devices and uses UDP.

q: Which sensor is commonly used to measure the intensity of ambient light?
exp: An LDR changes its resistance with incident light; the others sense temperature, magnetic field and pressure/vibration.

q: An Aadhaar number issued by UIDAI consists of how many digits?
exp: Aadhaar is a 12-digit unique identification number.

q: Which of the following is a professional networking website?
exp: LinkedIn is designed for professional networking and recruitment.

q: Which problem of cloud-only IoT is reduced by edge/fog computing?
options: High latency and bandwidth use because all raw data travels to a distant data centre
exp: Edge/fog nodes process data near the device, giving faster response and cutting bandwidth.

q: In IoT, edge computing refers to:
options: Storing all data permanently in a remote data centre
Connecting devices only through satellite links
Processing data close to where it is generated instead of sending everything to a central cloud
Encrypting data using only symmetric keys
exp: Edge computing reduces latency and bandwidth use by local processing.

q: Which consensus mechanism is used by the Bitcoin network?
exp: Bitcoin miners compete to solve a hash puzzle, which is Proof of Work.

q: In Hadoop's HDFS architecture, which node stores the file-system metadata (namespace and block locations)?
exp: The NameNode keeps metadata while DataNodes store the actual blocks.

q: Which technology allows two devices to exchange data when brought within a few centimetres of each other, as used in contactless payments?
exp: Near Field Communication works at about 4 cm at 13.56 MHz.

q: In electronic payment, a cash-like digital token (e-cash) system must especially prevent:
options: Double spending of the same token
exp: Digital cash is only data and can be copied, so the issuer must detect and prevent the same token being spent twice.

q: In the MQTT protocol, the server that receives messages from publishers and forwards them to the subscribed clients is called the:
exp: MQTT follows a publish-subscribe model mediated by a broker.

q: Which essential characteristic of cloud computing means resources can be automatically scaled up and down with demand?
exp: Rapid elasticity lets capacity expand or shrink as demand changes.

q: EDI in e-commerce stands for:
exp: EDI is the computer-to-computer exchange of standardised business documents.

q: In data warehousing, ETL stands for:
exp: ETL pulls data from sources, cleans/transforms it and loads it into the warehouse.
